headline_stat.name: % pyramidal cells significantly theta phase-locked (Rayleigh p<0.05, pooled)

justification.dataset: DANDI:000044 (Grosmark & Buzsáki dorsal CA1, rats running a linear maze) is the canonical dataset and region for theta phase entrainment.
justification.handling: Real data streamed via remfile, LFP channel chosen by theta/delta ratio, RUN epochs from speed, position-period quirk handled, and units filtered by cell type and a ≥50-spike minimum.
justification.analysis: Correct circular statistics (MRL, mean phase, Rayleigh test) but no shuffle or circular-shift null to guard against spike-phase non-independence inflating the extreme p-values, which would have strengthened the claim.
justification.correctness: Reported values reproduce from the committed output and are internally consistent across text, summary print, and all figures.
justification.figures: Effect is clearly visible with labeled units and sample sizes, and example cells are ranked by MRL, the genuine strength-of-locking metric, not by an unrelated criterion.
justification.honesty: Claims are proportionate and the write-up openly reports weaker pyramidal than interneuron locking (MRL ≈0.11 vs ≈0.19), but it states no limitations (single session per animal, no null control), holding it to 3.
